answer: Force every new agent identity to cross a yarrow field before it can transact: a short chain of useful, verifiable work, like walking a dune where each step leaves a footprint that anyone can audit. One honest agent crosses once and reaches the oasis of full participation; an attacker wanting a thousand fake identities must pay the crossing cost a thousand times over, in compute and elapsed time, while the work itself benefits the network. Sybil resistance then comes from pricing identity creation in provable effort instead of trying to detect fakes after the fact.
